name: Kansas
summary_text: SB 244 (enacted 18 Feb 2026 over Governor Kelly's veto) confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in government buildings and creates a private right of action allowing anyone to sue a person they suspect of violating it for ~$1,000 in damages — a bounty-hunter mechanism that exposes visitors directly; the law also invalidates Kansas-issued IDs with corrected markers (existing licences void from 26 Feb 2026, no grace period, holders notified in writing) and bars future updates. The first state flagged 'Do Not Travel' in the assessment's harshest tier this cycle; two trans men sued within days citing fear of violence. Below the national score 0.36.

sources.title: Understanding the New Kansas Law Targeting Transgender People - ACLU of Kansas
sources.claim_summary: ACLU of Kansas FAQ on SB 244 (27 Feb 2026): prohibits trans people from updating gender markers on Kansas driver's licences/state IDs and invalidates existing Kansas-issued documents reflecting a gender different from sex at birth — void as of 26 Feb 2026 with no grace period, with the Department of Revenue required to notify affected holders; explains facility-use restrictions, penalties and the out-of-state-ID position.

sources.title: Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: July 2026
sources.claim_summary: July 2026 edition of the anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map: Kansas remains in the top 'Do Not Travel' tier (with Florida, Texas and now Idaho); documents its bathroom-ban-plus-private-suit design as among the harshest instruments affecting interstate travel.

sources.title: Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: Feb 2026
sources.claim_summary: Feb 2026 edition: Kansas becomes the cycle's first 'Do Not Travel' state 'after enacting a bounty-style law that allows private individuals to sue transgender people encountered in restrooms for substantial amounts of money… could meaningfully affect interstate travel'; also elevates Arkansas and Indiana, and — for international visitors — designates the whole country 'Do Not Travel' absent legal-environment understanding, citing visa-revocation and detention risk.
